title: pvGaussianResampling
body:
## pvGaussianResampling

Splats the input points into a uniform volume (vtkImageData, point array SplatterValues): each point adds a Gaussian kernel ScaleFactor × value × exp(ExponentFactor × r² / R²) to nearby voxels within radius R, and overlapping contributions are combined by the accumulation mode (ParaView default Max). Without a selected array, or with scale splats off, each point contributes the kernel alone, giving a smooth point-density field. Use it to turn scattered particles or measurements into a continuous field for contouring or volume rendering; use pvResampleToImage to sample an existing mesh instead.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The default 50 × 50 × 50 grid can be too coarse or too costly; choose ResamplingGrid deliberately, because time grows with the voxel count.
- Fill Volume Boundary (on by default) overwrites the outer layer of voxels with Fill Value, which can create artificial contours at the box faces.
- Points cannot splat into other processes' regions, so MPI results can differ near partition boundaries. Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `GaussianResampling`. Identity: `filters/GaussianSplatter`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the filter. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet). The input needs at least one point-centred array with 1 component. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `EllipiticalEccentricity` | Control the shape of elliptical splatting. Eccentricity is the ratio of the major axis (aligned along normal) to the minor (axes) aligned along other two axes. So Eccentricity gt 1 creates needles with the long axis in the direction of the normal; Eccentricity lt 1 creates pancakes perpendicular to the normal vector. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `EllipticalSplats` | Turn on/off the generation of elliptical splats. If normal warping is on, then the input normals affect the distribution of the splat. This boolean is used in combination with the Eccentricity ivar. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `EmptyCellValue` | Set the Null value for output points not receiving a contribution from the input points. (This is the initial value of the voxel samples.) | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `ExtenttoResample` | Set / get the (xmin,xmax, ymin,ymax, zmin,zmax) bounding box in which the sampling is performed. If any of the (min,max) bounds values are min >= max, then the bounds will be computed automatically from the input data. Otherwise, the user-specified bounds will be used. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":6,"minItems":6,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1,1,1,1]` |
| `FillValue` | Specify the cap value to use. (This instance variable only has effect if the ivar Capping is on.) | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `FillVolumeBoundary` | Turn on/off the capping of the outer boundary of the volume to a specified cap value. This can be used to close surfaces (after isosurfacing) and create other effects. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `GaussianExponentFactor` | Set / get the sharpness of decay of the splats. This is the exponent constant in the Gaussian equation. Normally this is a negative value. | `{"maximum":0.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `GaussianSplatRadius` | Radius of influence of each splat as a fraction of the longest side of the sampling box: 0.1 means 10 % of that length. Voxels farther away receive nothing; larger values give smoother, more overlapping fields and longer run times. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `ResampleField` | Choose a scalar array to splat into the output cells. If ignore arrays is chosen, point density will be counted instead. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE","REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `ResamplingGrid` | Set / get the dimensions of the sampling structured point set. Higher values produce better results but are much slower. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `ScaleFactor` | Multiply Gaussian splat distribution by this value. If ScalarWarping is on, then the Scalar value will be multiplied by the ScaleFactor times the Gaussian function. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `ScaleSplats` | Turn on/off the scaling of splats by scalar value. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `SplatAccumulationMode` | Specify the scalar accumulation mode. This mode expresses how scalar values are combined when splats are overlapped. The Max mode acts like a set union operation and is the most commonly used; the Min mode acts like a set intersection, and the sum is just weird. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Min","Max","Sum"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Min"` |
